text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London continued their upward move with front month May adding $40 to close at $1,805 per tonne, while July added $53 to close at $1,870 per tonne. Roasters dominated on the buy side, although trade and speculative interest was also noted.

Overall the outlook is bright with most analysts predicting even higher prices. Ivory Coast's Commodities Minister said in an interview that coffee output in October/September 1996/97 would be less than 5.0 million bags. However, this will have no impact on prices as nobody expected output to reach 5 million bags.

Arabica futures in New York took a breather after tempting another run at new highs. Jorge Cardenas, the general manager of Colombia's Coffee Federation, officially admitted that the Federation has enormous difficulties meeting its export commitments because of unusually tight supply. This is likely to continue to drive the market higher. However, a downward correction is overdue after the recent sharp rises.

In this context it should be noted that after Wednesday's close, the CSCE reported another rise in certified coffee stocks. The Green Coffee Association of New York will release its stock data for April on Thursday and estimates range from a slight decrease to a 250,000 to 300,000 bag increase. Last month, GCA reported stocks of coffee stored in US warehouses rose by 111,000 bags in March, to 1.657 million bags.
May added 50 points to close at 261.50 cents/lb, while July lost 55 points to close at 240.60 cents/lb. The outer months closed 0.30 to 6.00 cents/lb higher.

BURUNDI - According to official sources, coffee production in Burundi in 1996/97 (October/September) could reach 417,000 60-kg bags, roughly the same what was produced the previous year. The production estimate is at odds with exports as reported by the International Coffee Organization, which point to a significantly lower crop this year. All the same the official production figure could be realistic and quite a bit of coffee may have left the country illegally.

Official sources said that Burundi has sold most of its coffee despite a trade embargo imposed on the country by regional leaders since last July. According to the Burundi Coffee Office (Ocibu) 287,000 60-kg bags have been sold so far, of which 251,000 bags were fully washed arabicas.
UNITED STATES - The CSCE reported certified coffee stocks increased by 2,375 60-kg bags to 35,412 bags as of May 13. There were 15,790 bags of coffee pending grading, the Exchange said.

MEXICO - Mexico exported 451,590 60-kg bags of coffee in April 1997, down 14.6 per cent from 529,015 bags a year ago, the government's Mexican Coffee Council said. Total exports in October/April 1996/97 reached 3.71 million bags. Mexican coffee exports in 1995/96 (October/April) totalled 3.47 million bags. The group is predicting a coffee harvest of 5.10 million bags this season, down from 5.37 million bags harvested the previous year.

HONDURAS - The Honduran Coffee Institute indicated that production in 1996/97 (October/September) may not reach the predicted 2.1 million 60-kg bags. Originally the crop was estimated at 2.3 million bags, but the institute lowered the estimate by 200,000 bags when heavy rains in September wiped out roads and damaged cherries in coffee growing areas.
